title: Skills can be static and dynamic context
caption: A useful split: standing context and information a platform adds as a task unfolds.

analogy.label: In the story:
analogy.text: Before the dive: your orders, the brief and the index. During it: the card and everything the robot sends up.

window.label: The context window at the end of the dive, top to bottom

skills.coding: skill metadata, if the app exposes it

memory.chat: your standing orders and the project brief
memory.coding: configured instruction files; loading varies by app

dynamic.label: Dynamic
dynamic.text: added as the task goes on; app-dependent

footer.chat: A skill's instructions may be added when you call it or when a platform activates it.
footer.ruleOfThumb: Static has exceptions, so take the split as a rule of thumb.
footer.coding: When you call /collect-sediment-sample or Claude Code activates it, its SKILL.md instructions enter the context.
footer.exceptions: .claude/rules/ files with paths load only when matching files open; Gemini CLI loads further GEMINI.md files just in time; a skill set to user-only invocation keeps even its name and description out.

alt.room: The control room at the end of the dive. On the wall: the live camera feed from the robot at the seabed, the project brief and the manual on its shelf with its index page facing out. At the desk the pilot sits; on the desk his notebook of standing orders, and everything that arrived during the dive: the pulled procedure card, Collect sediment sample, propped and lit; printed camera frames; a sonar strip; and a sample log on a clipboard.

static-and-dynamic-as-google-defines-the.header: Static and dynamic, as Google frames them
static-and-dynamic-as-google-defines-the.description: Google's whitepaper distinguishes standing context—such as system instructions, rule files, memory and persona definitions—from context added on demand, such as skill instructions, tool results, retrieved documents and windowed session history [1]. This is Google's framing of agent context, not a universal runtime guarantee or a measured result.

google-day-1-new-sdlc.title: Osmani, Saboo and Kartakis, The New SDLC With Vibe Coding (Google whitepaper, Kaggle)

why-static-and-dynamic-context-are-kept-.header: Why static and dynamic context are kept apart
why-static-and-dynamic-context-are-kept-.description: Day 1 says static context “is expensive because every token is present in every interaction, regardless of relevance”, and that too much of it “wastes tokens and dilutes signals” while too little “means the agent forgets critical rules” [1]. Day 3 repeats the split for the two files: “From one side AGENTS.md is always loaded within the project; Skills load on demand.” [2]

static-instructions-are-a-rule-of-thumb.description: Instruction files are not always present in every request. Claude Code .claude/rules/ files with paths load only when matching files open [1], Gemini CLI loads further GEMINI.md files just in time when a tool touches a directory [2], and Copilot path-specific instructions apply by file match [3]. Claude Code can expose skill names and descriptions for discovery, unless a skill is set to user-only invocation [4]. These are product-specific behaviours.

back-to-the-window.title: Back to the window
back-to-the-window.script: Some of you have seen the context window Explorable, where we looked at everything the model holds in its head at once. This is the same context window, and now we place skills in it.

the-standing-part.title: The standing part
the-standing-part.script: Start with the context that may be there before a task begins, in the order the Explorable shows it: system instructions, skill metadata when the app exposes it, and project instructions when configured. On our ship that is the standing rules, the manual's index, and your standing orders and project brief. Treat this as a useful sketch, not a guarantee about every app or request.

filling-as-you-dive.title: Filling as you dive
filling-as-you-dive.script: Then the task begins and the context can grow: a skill's instructions, if the app activates it, and tool results such as camera frames, sonar readings and sample logs. The exact loading path differs by product. A skill's metadata and full instructions can therefore appear at different points, depending on how that app handles them.
